name: Qatadah ibn Di'amah al-Sadusi
nameAr: قتادة بن دعامة بن قتادة السدوسي، أبو الخطاب، البصري
bornNote: 60 or 61 AH (Shamela record); said to have been born blind (Taqrib)
diedNote: “a dozen-odd” years after 100 AH (Taqrib); 117 or 118 are given, Ibn Hibban: died at Wasit in 117

taqrib.ar: ثقة ثبت، يقال ولد أكمه، وهو رأس الطبقة الرابعة
taqrib.en: Reliable and firm; it is said he was born blind; he heads the fourth generation.

teachers.name: Anas ibn Malik
teachers.source: Sahih al-Bukhari 15 (second chain); Sunan al-Nasa'i 5013: “he heard Anas”

students.name: Hammam ibn Yahya
students.source: Ibn Hajar, Hady al-Sari, ch. 9, letter ha'

verdicts.en: Qatadah has the best memory of anyone.

verdicts.ar: ما رأيت الذي هو أحفظ منه ولا أجدر أن يؤدي الحديث كما سمعه
verdicts.en: I have not seen anyone with a better memory, or more apt to deliver a hadith exactly as he heard it.

verdicts.ar: كان قتادة أحفظ أهل البصرة، لا يسمع شيئا إلا حفظه
verdicts.en: Qatadah had the best memory in Basra; he heard nothing without memorising it.

verdicts.ar: كان ثقة مأمونا حجة في الحديث، وكان يقول بشيء من القدر
verdicts.en: He was reliable, trustworthy, a proof in hadith; and he held something of the Qadari view.

verdicts.ar: لم يثبت عندنا عن قتادة القول بالقدر
verdicts.en: The Qadari view has not been established, to our satisfaction, of Qatadah.

verdicts.ar: أحد الأثبات المشهورين، كان يضرب به المثل في الحفظ، إلا أنه كان ربما دلس، وقال ابن معين: رمي بالقدر … احتج به الجماعة
verdicts.en: One of the famous firm narrators, proverbial for memory, except that he sometimes practised tadlis; Ibn Ma'in said he was accused of Qadar. All six relied on him.

tadlis.type: Tadlis al-isnad; “famous for tadlis, so described by al-Nasa'i and others”
tadlis.note: Ibn Hajar places him in the third rank, whose “from” is not accepted unless hearing is stated. Two things neutralise this for hadith 15: Shu'bah, who transmits from him there, said he had spared his hearers the tadlis of al-A'mash, Abu Ishaq and Qatadah by taking from them only what they heard (Tabaqat al-Mudallisin, closing section), and al-Nasa'i 5013 has the same route with “Qatadah, that he heard Anas”.

flags.label: Qadar accusation, disputed
flags.detail: Ibn Ma'in and Ibn Sa'd report that he held something of the Qadari view; Abu Dawud said it was not established. Ibn Hajar records both and notes that all six compilers relied on him (Hady al-Sari, ch. 9).

flags.label: Named only “Qatadah”
flags.detail: The name is unambiguous in the Sahih: the only other Qatadah among al-Bukhari's narrators is the Companion Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man, of a different generation.

bio: The blind Basran scholar whom Ibn Hajar made the head of the fourth generation, proverbial for memory and a leading commentator on the Qur'an. He heard Anas and was the teacher of Shu'bah, Hammam and Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah among many others. His habit of tadlis is the one caution attached to his “from”, and in hadith 15 it is removed by the identity of his student and by al-Nasa'i's wording.

sources.label: Ibn Hajar, Tabaqat al-Mudallisin, third rank, no. 92 (Shamela)
